abstract: We have analyzed the glycolipid markers of a recently cloned human embryonal carcinoma (EC) cell line, NTERA-2, which differentiates extensively into a variety of somatic cell types when exposed to retinoic acid. These tumor cells provide a model system that can be used to study the ontogeny of glycolipid diversity during human embryonic development. Glycolipid antigens were identified by cell surface immunofluorescence and thin-layer chromatography immunostaining using a comprehensive set of anticarbohydrate monoclonal antibodies. Undifferentiated NTERA-2 cells were found to express predominantly globo-series glycolipids, including Gb3, Gb5 (IV3GalGb4), globo-ganglioside (IV3NeuAc alpha 2----3GalGb4), globo-H (IV3Fuc alpha 1----2GalGb4), and globo-A (IV3GalNAc alpha 1----3[Fuc alpha 1----2]GalGb4). When NTERA-2 cells were induced to differentiate by culturing in the presence of 10(-5) M retinoic acid, a remarkable shift of cellular glycolipids from globo-series to lacto- and ganglio-series was observed: Globo-series structures declined, particularly during the period 7-20 days after first exposure to retinoic acid, while lacto-series structures, including fucosyl alpha 1----3 type 2 chain (Lex) and sialosyl type 2 chain, and ganglio-series structures, including GM3, GD3, 9-O-acetyl-GD3, GM2, GD2, and GT3, increased. The presence of globo-A and globo-H as the major ABH blood group antigens in undifferentiated NTERA-2 cells suggests that globo-series blood group antigens are embryonic antigens, synthesis of which switches to lacto-series during human development. Two-color immunofluorescence analysis indicated preferential expression of several ganglio- and lacto-series antigens on different subsets of differentiated cells and permitted the relationship of these subsets to the development of neurons in NTERA-2 cultures to be determined. The results suggest that glycosyltransferase, particularly those involved in controlling glycoconjugate core structure assembly, are key enzymes regulated during the differentiation of human EC cells and, by implication, during human embryogenesis.
abstract_ja: 最近クローニングされたヒト胎児性癌（EC）細胞株NTERA-2の糖脂質マーカーを解析した。NTERA-2はレチノイン酸に曝露すると、多様な体細胞へ広く分化する。糖脂質抗原は、一連の抗糖鎖モノクローナル抗体を用いて、細胞表面免疫蛍光および薄層クロマトグラフィー免疫染色により同定した。未分化NTERA-2細胞は主にglobo系糖脂質を発現しており、Gb3、Gb5（IV3GalGb4）、globo-ガングリオシド（IV3NeuAcα2→3GalGb4）、globo-H（IV3Fucα1→2GalGb4）、globo-A（IV3GalNAcα1→3[Fucα1→2]GalGb4）が含まれた。10^-5 Mのレチノイン酸存在下で分化を誘導すると、細胞糖脂質はglobo系からlacto系およびganglio系へ顕著に移行した。globo系構造は特に曝露後7〜20日の間に減少し、Lex、シアリルII型鎖などのlacto系構造と、GM3、GD3、9-O-アセチルGD3、GM2、GD2、GT3などのganglio系構造が増加した。未分化細胞に多いglobo-Aおよびglobo-Hは主要なABH血液型抗原であり、globo系血液型抗原が胚性抗原であって、ヒトの発生過程でlacto系へ合成が切り替わることを示唆する。二色免疫蛍光解析では、分化細胞の異なるサブセットでganglio系・lacto系抗原が優先的に発現しており、これらのサブセットとNTERA-2培養におけるニューロンの発生との関係を明らかにできた。これらの結果は、糖鎖コア構造の構築を制御する糖転移酵素が、ヒトEC細胞の分化、ひいてはヒト胚発生の過程で重要な制御酵素であることを示している。
